review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς οὖσιν [ἐν Ἐφέσῳ] καὶ πιστοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
1:1.targetText: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, to the holy ones who are in Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus:

groups.note: The dative substantival adjective πιστοῖς identifies the faithful recipients; English supplies to the faithful for that nominal case construction.

review.note: The pinned N1904 brackets ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, but the words are actually present in the installed source and LSV and have exact anchors. Jesus/Christ occur twice; each named occurrence remains tied to its own source token despite the first title’s different order.

1:2.sourceText: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:2.targetText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!

1:3.sourceText: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ εὐλογήσας ἡμᾶς ἐν πάσῃ εὐλογίᾳ πνευματικῇ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ,
1:3.targetText: Blessed [is] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us in every spiritual blessing in the heavenly [places] in Christ,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
Bracketed English noun completes the substantival heavenly phrase; N1904 has the plural adjective ἐπουρανίοις without a separate places noun.

1:4.sourceText: καθὼς ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ
1:4.targetText: according as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, for our being holy and unblemished before Him, in love,

groups.note: The infinitive εἶναι with accusative subject ἡμᾶς expresses the intended being-holy outcome, rendered for our being; the same us becomes possessive our before the English gerund.

1:5.sourceText: προορίσας ἡμᾶς εἰς υἱοθεσίαν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς αὐτόν, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ,
1:5.targetText: having foreordained us to the adoption of sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,

groups.note: The compound noun υἱοθεσία denotes adoption/placement as sons; the whole English adoption of sons renders that single kinship noun.

N1904 αὐτόν is the third-person pronoun in the to-Him relation; LSV uses the same-person reflexive Himself, interpreting its referent as the predestining subject rather than adding a different participant.

1:6.sourceText: εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἧς ἐχαρίτωσεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Ἠγαπημένῳ,
1:6.targetText: to the praise of the glory of His grace, in which He made us accepted in the beloved,

groups.note: ἐχαρίτωσεν denotes graciously favoring/bestowing favor on us; LSV expands the favoring predicate as He made ... accepted. This is the full favored/accepted relation, not an isolated Greek make verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness relative construction: LSV in which follows TR ἐν ᾗ; N1904 has the genitive relative ἧς without a separate ἐν here. The actual later ἐν stays with in the beloved.

1:7.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν διὰ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν παραπτωμάτων, κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ
1:7.targetText: in whom we have the redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of the trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:8.sourceText: ἧς ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ φρονήσει
1:8.targetText: in which He abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence,

groups.note: The genitive relative ἧς refers to the preceding grace, by attraction to its antecedent. LSV uses in which with the intransitive abounded wording; in is part of that English relative/sphere construction, not a separately printed Greek ἐν.

Greek περισσεύω supports an abounding/lavishing action; LSV takes the grace-relative phrase as its sphere and renders He abounded. This does not settle the alternative transitive reading which He lavished upon us.

1:9.sourceText: γνωρίσας ἡμῖν τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν αὐτοῦ, ἣν προέθετο ἐν αὐτῷ
1:9.targetText: having made known to us the secret of His will, according to His good pleasure, that He purposed in Himself,

groups.note: Greek αὐτῷ is a third-person dative pronoun; LSV takes it as coreferent with the purposing subject and renders Himself. The reflexive English form identifies that interpretation without asserting a separately printed ἑαυτῷ.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:10.sourceText: εἰς οἰκονομίαν τοῦ πληρώματος τῶν καιρῶν, ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ, τὰ ἐπὶ τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· ἐν αὐτῷ,
1:10.targetText: in regard to the dispensation of the fullness of the times, to bring into one the whole in the Christ, both the things in the heavens, and the things on the earth—in Him;

groups.note: ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι denotes summing/gathering up under one head; LSV expands it as to bring into one. The one is part of this compound-verb rendering, not a separate Greek numeral.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness coordination difference: TR includes τε with the heavenly/earthly things, behind LSV both; pinned N1904 has no τε at that point. Its actual later καί remains linked to and.

1:11.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἐκληρώθημεν προορισθέντες κατὰ πρόθεσιν τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐνεργοῦντος κατὰ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ,
1:11.targetText: in whom also we obtained an inheritance, being foreordained according to the purpose of Him who is working all things according to the counsel of His will,

groups.note: The passive allotment/inheritance verb ἐκληρώθημεν is rendered we obtained an inheritance. The review retains this LSV interpretation of the allotted/inherited relation without claiming the Greek verb is an active obtained form.

1:12.sourceText: εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης αὐτοῦ τοὺς προηλπικότας ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ·
1:12.targetText: for our being to the praise of His glory, [even] those who first hoped in the Christ,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English explanatory even supplies an appositional transition; N1904 has no separate even particle before those who first hoped.

1:13.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ καὶ ὑμεῖς, ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς σωτηρίας ὑμῶν, ἐν ᾧ καὶ πιστεύσαντες ἐσφραγίσθητε τῷ Πνεύματι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῷ Ἁγίῳ,
1:13.targetText: in whom you also, having heard the word of the truth—the good news of your salvation—in whom also having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:14.sourceText: ὅς ἐστιν ἀρραβὼν τῆς κληρονομίας ἡμῶν, εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῆς περιποιήσεως, εἰς ἔπαινον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.
1:14.targetText: which is a deposit of our inheritance, to the redemption of the acquired possession, to the praise of His glory.

groups.note: N1904 uses masculine relative ὅς, whereas LSV which neutrally refers to the same preceding Spirit/deposit context and TR has neuter ὅ. The grammatical-gender/relative-form difference is recorded without assigning a different participant.

1:15.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο κἀγώ, ἀκούσας τὴν καθ’ ὑμᾶς πίστιν ἐν τῷ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τὴν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους,
1:15.targetText: Because of this I also, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus, and the love to all the holy ones,

groups.note: The phrase καθ’ ὑμᾶς qualifies the faith as on your part/among you, rendered your faith. The preposition and participant pronoun together express the English possessive, not an isolated κατά = your equation.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:16.sourceText: οὐ παύομαι εὐχαριστῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν μνείαν ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου,
1:16.targetText: do not cease giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness object difference: LSV of you after mention follows the second TR ὑμῶν. N1904 has no second pronoun with mention; its actual ὑμῶν remains linked to the earlier for you.

1:17.sourceText: ἵνα ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ Πατὴρ τῆς δόξης, δώῃ ὑμῖν πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως ἐν ἐπιγνώσει αὐτοῦ,
1:17.targetText: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of the glory, may give to you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the recognition of Him,

1:18.sourceText: πεφωτισμένους τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν, εἰς τὸ εἰδέναι ὑμᾶς τίς ἐστιν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς κλήσεως αὐτοῦ, τίς ὁ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τῆς κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις,
1:18.targetText: the eyes of your understanding being enlightened, for your knowing what is the hope of His calling, and what the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the holy ones,

groups.note: The accusative subject ὑμᾶς of the knowing infinitive is rendered possessive your in for your knowing; the same recipients remain the knowers.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness noun difference: N1904 τῆς καρδίας means of the heart, whereas LSV of understanding follows TR τῆς διανοίας. The unlike heart/understanding nominal phrases are not treated as lexical identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: The first LSV of belongs to the differing understanding phrase, following TR τῆς διανοίας rather than N1904 τῆς καρδίας. Its differing head and genitive construction are left unpaired while the actual your pronoun is retained.
Source-witness noun difference: LSV understanding follows TR διανοίας, whereas N1904 has καρδίας, heart.
Source-witness connective difference: TR has καί before the second what, behind LSV and; N1904 has no conjunction there.

1:19.sourceText: καὶ τί τὸ ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ κράτους τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ,
1:19.targetText: and what the exceeding greatness of His power to us who are believing, according to the working of the power of His might,

1:20.sourceText: ἣν ἐνήργηκεν ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ ἐγείρας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ καθίσας ἐν δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις
1:20.targetText: which He worked in the Christ, having raised Him out of the dead, and sat [Him] at His right hand in the heavenly [places],

groups.note: The one actual αὐτόν is the shared object of raised and seated; LSV repeats that same participant in brackets after sat. Both English Him mentions remain anchored to this genuine shared pronoun.
Greek καθίσας is the active seating participle, having seated Him; LSV uses transitive sat [Him]. This is not the intransitive claim that the Father himself sat down.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English places completes the substantival heavenly phrase; Greek has no separate places noun.

1:21.sourceText: ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας καὶ δυνάμεως καὶ κυριότητος καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματος ὀνομαζομένου οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι·
1:21.targetText: far above all principality, and authority, and might, and lordship, and every name named, not only in this age, but also in the coming one;

groups.note: The substantival article/participle τῷ μέλλοντι denotes the coming [age], rendered the coming one. One expresses its nominal function and refers to the previously named age; no separate Greek numeral or one noun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:22.sourceText: καὶ πάντα ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν κεφαλὴν ὑπὲρ πάντα τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ,
1:22.targetText: and He put all things under His feet, and gave Him—head over all things to the Assembly,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:23.sourceText: ἥτις ἐστὶν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν πληρουμένου.
1:23.targetText: which is His body, the fullness of Him who is filling all in all.

groups.note: The substantival middle/passive-form participle τοῦ ... πληρουμένου is read by LSV as of Him who is filling. The review preserves that active/agentive interpretation and its real filling lexeme without settling alternative voice/interpretive analyses.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
